newsitem.title: INDIA: India ruling party splits as rebels break away.
newsitem.headline: India ruling party splits as rebels break away.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party split on Saturday as supporters of party president Laloo Prasad Yadav declared the formation of a breakaway group, witnesses said.

They said the group had been named Rashtriya (National) Janata Dal by supporters of Yadav, who had led a boycott of the party's presidential election ballot on Thursday. The Janata Dal heads India's ruling 15-party United Front coalition.

"This convention renames Janata Dal as Rashtriya Janata Dal," Ram Chandra Purve, a supporter of Laloo Yadav from his eastern state of Bihar, told hundreds of assembled supporters in the Indian capital.

Yadav, chief minister of Bihar, boycotted the Janata Dal party's official election, saying voter lists had been rigged to favour his challenger, Sharad Yadav. Results of the balloting is expected on Sunday.

Laloo Yadav has said he would continue support to Gujral's government. His differences are essentially with former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who is accused by Laloo Yadav's supporters of unfairly opposing their leader.
Laloo Yadav is believed to control at least 16 of the 45 party lawmakers in the lower house of the federal parliament, which has 545 members.
